items.title: The portal and the mailbox
items.text: aol.com still publishes news and still delivers mail. Announcing its purchase in October 2025, Bending Spoons’ chief executive said AOL had “around 8 million daily and 30 million monthly active users.”[^21] In 2026 the new owner said it had moved the portal to a new content system and rebuilt the webmail front end.[^20]

items.title: Dial-up
items.text: Discontinued on September 30, 2025, with the AOL Dialer software and the AOL Shield browser.[^18] The Associated Press, citing Census Bureau data, reported that an estimated 163,401 U.S. households used only dial-up in 2023. How many of them were AOL’s is unknown.[^30]

items.title: AOL Instant Messenger
items.text: More than 61 million registered users in June 2000.[^5] Closed on December 15, 2017.[^27]

items.title: The media brands
items.text: Verizon’s 2015 announcement listed The Huffington Post, TechCrunch and Engadget among AOL’s assets.[^15] They passed to Oath and then to Apollo’s Yahoo with the rest of Verizon’s media business.[^28][^16] Patch, the local news network, had already been moved into a joint venture majority-owned by Hale Global in January 2014.[^14]

items.title: The parent
items.text: AOL Time Warner became Time Warner on October 16, 2003.[^7] It distributed AOL to shareholders in 2009.[^12] The SEC now lists the old registrant under the name Warner Media, LLC.[^6]

items.title: The voice
items.text: Elwood Edwards, who recorded “You’ve Got Mail” in 1989, died in November 2024 at 74.[^26]

blocks.title: Who has owned the AOL name
blocks.subtitle: Five owners in forty-one years. Each paid for something different.

nodes.what: Incorporated May 24, 1985. Renamed America Online, Inc. in 1991 and listed in 1992.[^1][^32]
AOL’s shareholders take about 55% of the merged company. “AOL” leaves the name in October 2003.[^5][^6][^7]
nodes.price: about $147 billion recorded as the cost of acquiring Time Warner

nodes.what: Spun off to Time Warner’s shareholders as an independent, listed company with 5.0 million subscribers.[^12]
Agreed May 12, 2015. Combined with Yahoo as Oath in June 2017.[^15][^28]
Buys Verizon’s media business, AOL and Yahoo together. Verizon keeps 10%.[^16][^17]
Acquires AOL Holdco I LLC from Yahoo three months after dial-up ends.[^19][^21]

blocks.source: Company filings and announcements as cited. The 2001 figure is the accounting cost of Time Warner to AOL, not a price paid for AOL.
